apiDescriptions./shipping: A fictional shipping API for Trailhead Supply. Explore fixed shipping quotes, shipment creation and cancellation, tracking snapshots, and a text-only demonstration label. These static examples do not buy postage, move parcels, store shipments, or contact carriers. POST bodies are optional; supplied non-empty JSON is syntax-checked, but field values and query strings never select responses. Explicit demo-faults routes cover invalid parcels, carrier outages, rate limiting, a delayed HTTP 504, and connection failure.

endpoints.name: Shipping API health
endpoints.description:
Description:
Let a fulfillment dashboard or support agent check that the Trailhead Supply shipping mock is reachable without inspecting shipments or requesting rates.

Technical implementation:
HEAD returns a fixed 200 OK with sample headers and no response body. This is a mock endpoint subject to instance API-key protection, not a live carrier or dependency check. GET is not configured.

endpoints.name: Compare shipping rates
endpoints.description:
Description:
Help a Trailhead Supply shopper compare delivery cost and estimated arrival time when choosing between standard and express shipping at checkout.

Technical implementation:
Returns fixed standard and express quotes in USD for a fictional 1.2 kg parcel. Query strings do not change the destination, weight, currency, or prices.

endpoints.name: Create a sample shipment
endpoints.description:
Description:
Demonstrate preparing a paid order for dispatch by giving warehouse staff a shipment reference, tracking number, and label link.

Technical implementation:
Simulates shipment creation with 201 Created and a resolvable Location header. Returns fixed tracking and label links regardless of body fields; no shipment, postage, or carrier booking is created.

endpoints.name: Inspect the sample shipment
endpoints.description:
Description:
Let a fulfillment dashboard or support agent review the selected delivery service and find the tracking and label details for a sample order.

Technical implementation:
GET returns the fixed shipment. The lookup exists before creation and remains unchanged after cancellation.

endpoints.name: Track the sample shipment
endpoints.description:
Description:
Show a shopper that their order has a shipping label but has not yet progressed through delivery, setting expectations on the order-tracking page.

Technical implementation:
Returns a fixed label-created tracking snapshot with a fictional timestamp. Polling does not advance the shipment; the delivered route is a separate, explicitly selected fixture.

endpoints.name: Inspect a delivered tracking scenario
endpoints.description:
Description:
Demonstrate the completed-delivery view a shopper or support agent sees after a parcel reaches its destination, including a short journey history.

Technical implementation:
Always returns a separate fictional delivered tracking history. It does not represent a state change to TRACK-DEMO-001 and contains no customer address or signature.

response.body: {"trackingId":"TRACK-DEMO-DELIVERED","status":"delivered","events":[{"status":"in_transit","timestamp":"2026-01-05T15:00:00Z","description":"The demonstration parcel left the sample depot."},{"status":"delivered","timestamp":"2026-01-07T10:00:00Z","description":"The demonstration parcel was delivered."}]}

endpoints.name: Download a demonstration label
endpoints.description:
Description:
Demonstrate the warehouse workflow for downloading a parcel label before packing and dispatch, using a clearly marked demonstration document.

Technical implementation:
Returns a text-only attachment to test non-JSON download handling. This is not a PDF, barcode, postage purchase, or valid shipping label.

response.body:
MOCK SHIPPING LABEL
Shipment: shp-demo-001
Tracking: TRACK-DEMO-001
Service: standard
Not valid for shipment.

endpoints.name: Cancel the sample shipment
endpoints.description:
Description:
Demonstrate withdrawing a shipment request when an order is canceled or its delivery arrangements need to be changed before dispatch.

Technical implementation:
Simulates cancellation with 204 No Content. Nothing is canceled or deleted; repeated calls succeed and shipment, tracking, and label lookups remain unchanged.

endpoints.name: Shipment validation fault demo
endpoints.description:
Description:
Help warehouse staff recognize and correct an invalid parcel weight before they can complete a shipping booking.

Technical implementation:
Always returns a static 422 parcel-weight error after global JSON syntax checks. No parcel or address fields are inspected; malformed JSON instead receives the runtime's 400 response.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Unprocessable Entity","status":422,"detail":"The sample parcel weight is invalid.","errors":{"parcelWeightKg":["Parcel weight must be greater than zero."]}}

endpoints.name: Carrier outage fault demo
endpoints.description:
Description:
Exercise the fulfillment experience when a carrier cannot accept bookings, so staff see a temporary service problem rather than a successful dispatch confirmation.

Technical implementation:
Always returns 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After: 15. No carrier is contacted and waiting does not change this configured failure.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Service Unavailable","status":503,"detail":"The sample carrier booking service is unavailable. Retry later."}

endpoints.name: Look up a missing tracking number
endpoints.description:
Description:
Demonstrate helping a shopper who enters an unrecognized tracking number, prompting them to check the reference from their order confirmation.

Technical implementation:
The literal unknown tracking route always returns a configured 404 problem response. Other unconfigured tracking numbers receive MockAPI's ordinary unmatched response; no tracking service is queried.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Not Found","status":404,"detail":"The sample tracking number does not exist.","trackingId":"unknown"}

endpoints.name: Tracking rate-limit fault demo
endpoints.description:
Description:
Exercise a tracking page that is refreshed too frequently, so the shopper is asked to wait briefly instead of repeatedly contacting the delivery service.

Technical implementation:
The first two requests in a rolling 10-second window return a fixed label-created snapshot. Further requests return 429 with Retry-After: 10. The dashboard preselects three calls; counters are process-local and tracking state never changes.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Too Many Requests","status":429,"detail":"The sample tracking request limit was exceeded. Retry in 10 seconds."}

endpoints.name: Carrier timeout fault demo
endpoints.description:
Description:
Demonstrate the experience when a carrier takes too long to provide an update, allowing the tracking page to explain the delay and offer a later retry.

Technical implementation:
Waits one second, then sends an explicit HTTP 504 problem response. This is a delayed server response, not a client-side timeout, DNS failure, or actual carrier request.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Gateway Timeout","status":504,"detail":"The sample carrier did not respond before the fictional gateway deadline."}

endpoints.name: Carrier connection fault demo
endpoints.description:
Description:
Exercise an interrupted connection to the delivery service so the shopper sees a recoverable connection problem instead of an incorrect shipment status.

Technical implementation:
Immediately aborts the accepted connection without sending an HTTP response. It approximates a transport failure but does not reproduce DNS or TLS failures and never contacts a carrier.
